statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma: Let O be a fixed language with a deterministic decider using time and space at most q(l) on queries of length l. Suppose a uniform one-pass machine uses space at most S(m); on every length-2^m input, each transition including final reporting takes at most T(m) time, constructs queries of length at most L(m), and makes at most r(m) oracle queries. Replacing its oracle queries to O with that decider yields an oracle-free uniform machine with space S(m)+O(q(L(m))+L(m)) and per-transition time O(T(m)+r(m)(q(L(m))+L(m))). Proof: simulate the original transition and retain its configuration and query work tape. For each query, run the fixed decider and feed back its answer. The query occupies O(L(m)) space and the decider uses at most q(L(m)) space, giving the stated additive space bound. The original transition costs at most T(m); the query deciders add at most r(m)q(L(m)) time, while constructing and handling the queries is covered by O(T(m)+r(m)L(m)). The same argument applies to final reporting by hypothesis. Since each component is fixed and uniform, the composition is uniform. Thus the conclusion follows.
derivation: The machine's transition computation and each oracle query are explicitly simulated in sequence. For each query, its length is at most L(m); the fixed decider therefore uses time and space at most q(L(m)). Summing over at most r(m) queries gives the additive time bound and the maximum simultaneous decider/query workspace gives the additive space bound. The final-report transition is covered by the same assumptions.

statement: Lemma (polynomial-time oracle elimination with explicit query bounds). Let s(m)≥2. Let M be a uniform one-pass oracle machine whose space is S(m), whose time per input-read interval and final report is at most T(m), and which makes at most r(m) oracle queries in each such interval. Suppose every query has length at most L(m), and a fixed uniform decider for the oracle language runs in time and space O(ℓ^k) on queries of length ℓ, for a fixed k≥1. Then M has an oracle-free uniform simulation with space S(m)+O(L(m)^k+L(m)) and per-interval and final-report time O(T(m)+r(m)(L(m)^k+L(m))). In particular, if S,T,r,L are each bounded by a fixed power of s, then the simulation also has space and per-interval time bounded by fixed powers of s. Proof: Simulate each interval of M and, whenever it issues a query, run the fixed decider on that query and return its answer. A query and its decider use O(L^k+L) additional space; queries are answered sequentially, so this workspace is not multiplied by r. Their total time per interval is O(r(L^k+L)), in addition to M’s interval time T. The same simulation applies to the final report under the stated bounds. The fixed decider and M are uniform, so their composition is uniform. Substituting polynomial-in-s bounds gives polynomial-in-s resources.
derivation: Sequentially replace each oracle answer with the fixed decider’s answer. Sum the decider time over at most r queries; take the maximum, not sum, of its workspace because queries are handled sequentially. Include final reporting in the same per-interval accounting.

statement: Conditional lemma (eliminating the fixed PH oracle under P=NP). Fix A in PH and suppose P=NP. Then the fixed language Sigma_3SAT^A is in P. Consequently, any uniform one-pass machine using this oracle, with query lengths and number of queries per input-read interval and final report bounded by fixed powers of s(m), and with original space and per-interval time bounded by fixed powers of s(m), has an oracle-free uniform simulation whose space and per-interval time are also bounded by fixed powers of s(m). Proof: Since A is in PH, each predicate testing membership in A is expressible by a fixed finite block of polynomially bounded quantifiers with a polynomial-time predicate. A Sigma_3SAT^A instance asks whether a polynomially bounded quantified computation with polynomially many A queries accepts. Replace each A query by its fixed PH definition; the resulting language remains in PH by closure under polynomial-time reductions and finite quantifier-block composition. P=NP implies PH=P by induction on the hierarchy levels, so Sigma_3SAT^A has a fixed uniform polynomial-time decider. Apply sequential oracle elimination: each query of length L(m) is decided in polynomial time and space in L(m); summing time over polynomially many queries per interval and reusing the decider workspace gives polynomial-in-s resources. The final report is covered by the same query bounds. This is conditional and does not assert that any particular MMW machine satisfies those bounds.
derivation: Under P=NP, PH collapses to P. For fixed A in PH, the fixed finite-level oracle computation defining Sigma_3SAT^A can be expanded into a finite PH quantifier description, hence is in P. Substitute that decider for each query, answering sequentially; polynomially bounded query size and count preserve polynomial-in-s update time and space.

lemma: LEMMA (Class inclusion for the forward direction of Proposition 13). Let s be time-constructible, s(m) ≥ m, A ∈ PH. Let M_{s,A}^{plain} be the class of uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithms without oracle access, with space S_M(m) and update time τ_M(m). Let ALG_{s,A} be the uniform one-pass streaming algorithm with Σ_3SAT^A oracle whose existence is guaranteed by MMW Theorem 1.2 (for the given s, A), with space S_{ALG}(m) = s(m)^{O(1)} and update time τ_{ALG}(m) = s(m)^{O(1)}. Assume P = NP. Then there exists a uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithm M* ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} (i.e., oracle-free) such that: (1) M* solves the same search problem as ALG_{s,A} (Search-MCSP^A[s]); (2) Space S_{M*}(m) = s(m)^{O(1)}; (3) Update time τ_{M*}(m) = s(m)^{O(1)}; (4) The O(1) exponents are fixed constants depending on the algorithm but not on m. Proof: 1. ALG_{s,A} is a uniform algorithm (single Turing/RAM machine for all input lengths). 2. Under P=NP, PH=P, so Σ_3SAT^A ∈ P (since A ∈ PH ⇒ PH^A = PH). 3. Σ_3SAT^A has a fixed uniform polynomial-time decider D. 4. ALG_{s,A} makes at most r(m) = s(m)^{O(1)} queries per update interval, each of length at most L(m) = s(m)^{O(1)}. 5. Replace each oracle call with a call to D. By sequential simulation (S0060/S0061), the space overhead is O(L(m)^k) = s(m)^{O(1)} and time overhead per interval is O(r(m) ⋅ L(m)^k) = s(m)^{O(1)}. 6. The resulting machine M* is uniform, one-pass, oracle-free, and has space S_{M*}(m) = s(m)^{O(1)}, update time τ_{M*}(m) = s(m)^{O(1)}. 7. M* ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} by definition (oracle-free uniform one-pass RAM). This lemma closes the class-inclusion gap for the forward direction (40a) ⇒ P≠NP by showing the uniform streaming algorithm from MMW Thm 1.2, after oracle elimination under P=NP, falls in M_{s,A}^{plain}. The gap G-new's reference to MMW Thm 1.3 concerns the converse direction (¬(40a) ⇒ ¬(8)), which uses Lemma 11 and Lemma 12 (RAM simulation + unrolling) rather than Thm 1.3.

proved_step: statement_start: LEMMA (Converse direction: ¬(40a) implies NP ⊆ P/poly, using Lemma 11+12 and MMW Thm 1.3). Let s: N→N be time-constructible with s(m) ≥ m. Let A ∈ PH. Assume ¬(40a), i.e., ∀ time-constructible s' ≥ m ∀ A' ∈ PH ∃ M ∈ M_{s',A'}^{plain} ∃ c,d ∈ N ∃ m0 ∀ m ≥ m0: S_M(m) ≤ s'(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s'(m)^d. Then NP ⊆ P/poly. Proof: 1. Since ¬(40a) holds for ALL s' ≥ m and ALL A' ∈ PH, instantiate it with s'(m) = m (which is time-constructible, m ≥ m) and the same A ∈ PH from the forward direction (any A ∈ PH works for MMW Thm 1.3). 2. ¬(40a) gives: ∃ M ∈ M_{m,A}^{plain} ∃ c,d ∈ N ∃ m0 ∀ m ≥ m0: S_M(m) ≤ m^c and τ_M(m) ≤ m^d. 3. M is a uniform deterministic one-pass RAM solving Search-MCSP^A[m] on truth-table streams of length N=2^m. 4. Lemma 11 (RAM → staged circuit): M can be exactly simulated by a uniform family of staged Boolean circuits {C_m} where C_m has N = 2^m stages (one per input bit). The state after t bits has width S_M(m) ≤ m^c. Each stage computes the next state (m^c bits) from the current state (m^c bits) plus the next input bit (1 bit). The transition function is a fixed Boolean circuit of size poly(m^c) = m^{O(1)} (uniform because M is uniform). 5. Lemma 12 (Staged → standard circuit): The staged circuit {C_m} with N stages of width w = m^c can be unrolled to a standard Boolean circuit of size N * w * poly(w) = 2^m * m^c * m^{O(1)} = 2^m * m^{O(1)} = N (log N)^{O(1)}. 6. This standard circuit family solves Search-MCSP^A[m] on inputs of length N=2^m with size N (log N)^k for some fixed k. 7. MMW Theorem 1.3 (or 1.4, Ilango FOCS 2020): For every A ∈ PH, if Search-MCSP^A[m^c] has general Boolean circuits of size N (log N)^k for all k, then NP ⊆ P/poly. Here we have it for s(m) = m and some fixed k. But the hypothesis of ¬(40a) gives us the machine M with some FIXED c,d. To get circuits for all k, we use the universal quantification in ¬(40a): for any target k, choose s'(m) = m^{k+1}. Then ¬(40a) gives M with S_M(m) ≤ m^{c(k+1)}, giving circuit size N * m^{c(k+1)} = N (log N)^{c(k+1)}. Since this works for every k, we get circuits of size N(log N)^k for all k. 8. By MMW Thm 1.3, this implies NP ⊆ P/poly. This completes the converse direction, and together with S0063/S0068 establishes the full equivalence in Proposition 13.

lemma: LEMMA (Exact quantifier structure of (40a) and its negation, with class matching). (40a) reads: ∀ s: ℕ→ℕ time-constructible with s(m) ≥ m, ∀ A ∈ PH, ∀ M ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain}, ∀ c,d ∈ ℕ, ∃ m₀ ∈ ℕ, ∀ m ≥ m₀: S_M(m) > s(m)^c ∨ τ_M(m) > s(m)^d. Its negation ¬(40a) is: ∃ s: ℕ→ℕ time-constructible with s(m) ≥ m, ∃ A ∈ PH, ∃ M ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain}, ∃ c,d ∈ ℕ, ∃ m₀ ∈ ℕ, ∀ m ≥ m₀: S_M(m) ≤ s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s(m)^d. The class M_{s,A}^{plain} is exactly the uniform deterministic one-pass oracle-free RAM algorithms solving Search-MCSP^A[s] on truth-table streams of length N=2^m. This matches the class quantified in the forward direction (S0068): under P=NP, the MMW Thm 1.2 algorithm (uniform, with Σ₃SAT^A oracle) simulates to an oracle-free M* ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} with S_M*(m) = s(m)^{O(1)}, τ_M*(m) = s(m)^{O(1)}, contradicting (40a). For the converse direction, ¬(40a) quantifies ∀s ≥ m, so we may instantiate with s'(m) = m^{k+1} for any target k ∈ ℕ, yielding a machine M with S_M(m) ≤ m^{c(k+1)}, τ_M(m) ≤ m^{d(k+1)}. By Lemma 11+12, this unrolls to circuits of size N·m^{O(k)} = N(log N)^{O(k)}. Since k is arbitrary, we obtain circuits of size N(log N)^k for all k, matching the hypothesis of MMW Thm 1.3 (which requires circuits for Search-MCSP^A[m^c] of size N(log N)^k for all k, for some c ≥ 1; here c = 1 works). Both directions are therefore valid with the exact quantifiers as written.

statement_start: LEMMA (Exact unrolling of a bounded-state one-pass machine). Let a deterministic machine read N input bits. Suppose each read-boundary configuration is encoded by at most w bits, each transition from a configuration and the next input bit is computed by a Boolean circuit of size at most T, and the final reporting function is computed by a Boolean circuit of size at most U. Then the machine’s exact output function has a Boolean circuit of size at most NT+U. Proof: create N copies of the transition circuit, connect each copy’s configuration output to the next copy’s configuration input, and feed input bit i to copy i. By induction on i, after copy i the wires encode the machine’s configuration after reading the first i bits. Feed the final configuration into the reporting circuit; it returns the machine’s exact output on every input. The total circuit size is at most NT+U.

The fixed-pair (40a) is: ∀M ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} ∀c,d ∈ ℕ ∃m₀ ∈ ℕ ∀m ≥ m₀: S_M(m) > s(m)^c ∨ τ_M(m) > s(m)^d. Its negation is logically equivalent to: ∃M ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} ∃c,d ∈ ℕ ∃m₀ ∈ ℕ ∀m ≥ m₀: S_M(m) ≤ s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s(m)^d, i.e., ∃M,c,d,m₀ B(M,c,d,m₀). Proof: The fixed-pair formula has quantifier prefix ∀M ∀c,d ∃m₀ ∀m≥m₀. Negation pushes through: ¬(∀M ∀c,d ∃m₀ ∀m≥m₀ P(M,c,d,m₀,m)) ≡ ∃M ∃c,d ∀m₀ ∃m≥m₀ ¬P(M,c,d,m₀,m) where P is the disjunction of strict bounds. But ¬(A>B ∨ C>D) ≡ (A≤B ∧ C≤D). So we get ∃M ∃c,d ∀m₀ ∃m≥m₀: S_M(m) ≤ s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s(m)^d. This is NOT the claimed B-form (which has ∃m₀ ∀m≥m₀). The lemma statement as originally given (S0074) is therefore FALSE: the negation of the fixed-pair (40a) does NOT assert a single tail threshold m₀ that works for all m; it only asserts that for EVERY m₀ there is some m≥m₀ where both bounds hold. This is a strictly weaker condition. The corrected lemma: The negation of the fixed-pair (40a) is ∃M ∃c,d ∀m₀ ∃m≥m₀: S_M(m) ≤ s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s(m)^d. This does not give a uniform tail bound. The universal quantifier over m₀ is essential and cannot be pulled inward. This explains why S0074's claim of '∃m₀ ∀m≥m₀' was incorrect — it confuses the negation of ∀∃ with ∃∀. The machine-class and oracle-free restrictions remain unchanged.
